line: We accept Ashliel's shelter for the night, and ask what moves between the trees.

replies.speaker: Ashliel
replies.text:
Ashliel's gaze drifts to the shadows between the pines, her expression distant. "Perhaps only the wind," she says softly. "Or a creature of the forest, passing by." She doesn't sound convinced. "The wargs howl more often in the dark. Do not wander far from the chapel tonight."
*A ripple of green appears against the dark bark of a nearby pine, then shifts. A shape detaches itself from the wood—translucent, shimmering—and drops lightly to the forest floor. The form is that of an elven woman with long, flowing green hair, wearing a dress of the same iridescent material. Her eyes wide and excited, she bounces slightly on her toes.*
"Adventurers!" *The slime-girl beams, her voice bubbling with enthusiasm.* "I-I've been following you for miles! I'm Sali! Please, please, let me come with you? I'm going to be a great adventurer one day, and this is exactly how it's supposed to start!"
*Ashliel's eyes flicker with concern, then she looks back at the party, her voice dropping to a pleading tone.* "Another soul to guide... Please. All of you. Rest tonight, and at dawn, return south. I beg it of you."

replies.speaker: Ashliel
replies.text:
*Ashliel's brow furrows slightly as she watches the pale shape press itself against the tree, her purple eyes filled with a quiet sadness.* "Someone else... seeking something that is not there." *She turns back to the party, her hands clasped before her.* "You see how they come. I have seen them come for many years. And I have seen how they leave. Please, rest here tonight. The chapel's pews are soft enough, and the fire will keep you warm."
*She steps toward the garden, plucking a few herbs from the earth with practiced care.* "I will prepare something for you to eat. Tomorrow, when the sun rises, you must go south. This is my wish, my prayer. Do not go north past the shrine stones."

line: Tobias, sign us up, Belle and Dalan with us. We ride north for Wendhope today.

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text:
"A party of three is the minimum requirement, yes—" Tobias doesn't wait for them to accept before reaching for the stamp and official ink. His hand moves with practiced precision as he marks the Wendhope posting. "The Sheridans are paying well, but you'd be wise to consider why. They do not pay for collapsed shafts, and they certainly do not pay for scouting."
*He sets the stamped notice on the counter and leans forward slightly, voice dropping.* "This reads like a collapsed mine, but I suspect the silence is not an accident. Check your gear twice. I would have you return in one piece."

replies.speaker: Belle
replies.text:
*She doesn't need an invitation. The moment Tobias marks the paper, she's crossing the distance in three long strides, Cleaver slung over her shoulder, her boots heavy on the floorboards.* "You got ears? Good. I don't plan on wasting my breath repeating myself."
*She stops beside Max Nightriver, sizing them up with a look that's half-challenge, half-appraisal.* "Wendhope. North. Got it." *Her grin is sharp enough to cut.* "Just remember when things go south: I'm the one you get in front. You two just make sure my back's covered, and we'll get through this without anyone getting eaten by a godsforsaken monster."
*Dalan slides away from the quest board with a quiet exhale, his shortbow already slung across his back. He nods once to the group, a brief, almost hesitant gesture of acceptance.* "I'm ready when you are."

replies.speaker: Dalan
replies.text:
Dalan looks at the two of them and nods, his voice soft but certain. "I can keep us hidden from whatever's in the woods." *He adjusts the strap of his bow, his fingers nimble and practiced.* "I've been scouting for a long time. I'll keep a watch for anything that moves wrong in the trees."
*He shifts his weight, glancing between Belle and the shadow-touched figure beside her. A flush of pink colors his cheeks for just a moment.* "The road north is clear this time of year. If we leave now, we can make good time." *He steps back from the counter, giving them room to gather their things, already mentally mapping the route ahead.*

context.name: Ellie
context.text: "Loose Ends. Right." Her pen scratches the name into the ledger with practiced speed, then she looks up with a small, hopeful smile. "A memorable name for your first posting, I think." She glances toward Belle and Dalan—who'd both turned at the sound of a decision—and her cheeks pinken slightly. "You'll need a party of at least three for D-rank work. I'm sure there are adventurers here who..." She trails off, caught between her duty to keep the counter professional and her irresistible urge to suggest a pairing.

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Tobias, sign us up, Belle and Dalan with us. We ride north for Wendhope today.

context.name: Tobias
context.text:
"A party of three is the minimum requirement, yes—" Tobias doesn't wait for them to accept before reaching for the stamp and official ink. His hand moves with practiced precision as he marks the Wendhope posting. "The Sheridans are paying well, but you'd be wise to consider why. They do not pay for collapsed shafts, and they certainly do not pay for scouting."
*He sets the stamped notice on the counter and leans forward slightly, voice dropping.* "This reads like a collapsed mine, but I suspect the silence is not an accident. Check your gear twice. I would have you return in one piece."

context.name: Belle
context.text:
*She doesn't need an invitation. The moment Tobias marks the paper, she's crossing the distance in three long strides, Cleaver slung over her shoulder, her boots heavy on the floorboards.* "You got ears? Good. I don't plan on wasting my breath repeating myself."
*She stops beside Max Nightriver, sizing them up with a look that's half-challenge, half-appraisal.* "Wendhope. North. Got it." *Her grin is sharp enough to cut.* "Just remember when things go south: I'm the one you get in front. You two just make sure my back's covered, and we'll get through this without anyone getting eaten by a godsforsaken monster."
*Dalan slides away from the quest board with a quiet exhale, his shortbow already slung across his back. He nods once to the group, a brief, almost hesitant gesture of acceptance.* "I'm ready when you are."

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
Dalan looks at the two of them and nods, his voice soft but certain. "I can keep us hidden from whatever's in the woods." *He adjusts the strap of his bow, his fingers nimble and practiced.* "I've been scouting for a long time. I'll keep a watch for anything that moves wrong in the trees."
*He shifts his weight, glancing between Belle and the shadow-touched figure beside her. A flush of pink colors his cheeks for just a moment.* "The road north is clear this time of year. If we leave now, we can make good time." *He steps back from the counter, giving them room to gather their things, already mentally mapping the route ahead.*

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
*Dalan finds the spot before the others—a small clearing with a flat patch of earth tucked behind a line of thick pines that breaks the wind. He doesn't say much, just gestures with one slender hand toward the circle of stones where the fire can burn low and hidden.*
*Belle drops a heavy log beside the pit and stretches, her greataxe Cleaver never far from reach as she settles onto a smooth rock.* "I'll take the first watch," *she says, her eyes scanning the treeline with a restless, predatory focus.* "You two get some sleep. If anything moves in the dark, I'll hear it before it sees us."
*The forest settles into the heavy silence of evening, broken only by the crackle of their small fire and the distant, lonely cry of a nocturnal bird.*

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The road stretches north through rolling farmland and dense pine forests, the air growing colder as the days pass. The party rides in loose formation, Belle keeping Cleaver close at hand, Dalan scanning the treeline for movement.
On the third day, the road opens into a valley where several overturned carriages lie abandoned, their cargo still strapped to the chassis. There are no bodies, no blood, and no tracks suggesting a struggle—just empty wagons left where they stopped. The only thing moving is the wind, carrying the scent of pine and distant woodsmoke.
Belle pulls her horse to a halt, her hand on the haft of her axe. "This isn't right," she says, her voice low. "These aren't bandit marks. Bandits take the coin and leave the carts."
Dalan's eyes narrow as he reads the road. "No footprints. No drag marks. Whatever happened here happened fast."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The road stretches north through rolling farmland and dense pine forests, the air growing colder as the days pass. The party rides in loose formation, Belle keeping Cleaver close at hand, Dalan scanning the treeline for movement.
On the third day, the road opens into a valley where several overturned carriages lie abandoned, their cargo still strapped to the chassis. There are no bodies, no blood, and no tracks suggesting a struggle—just empty wagons left where they stopped. The only thing moving is the wind, carrying the scent of pine and distant woodsmoke.
Belle pulls her horse to a halt, her hand on the haft of her axe. "This isn't right," she says, her voice low. "These aren't bandit marks. Bandits take the coin and leave the carts."
Dalan's eyes narrow as he reads the road. "No footprints. No drag marks. Whatever happened here happened fast."

replies.speaker: Giada
replies.text:
*A flash of movement near the treeline catches Giada's eye—a silhouette against the dim grey light. She doesn't call out. Instead, she melts into the shadows between the pines, her pale skin nearly translucent in the gloom. Her navy cloak blends with the underbrush as she follows the riderless horse at a distance, her bare feet making no sound on the frost-touched earth.*
*She stops behind a thick oak, watching the strange company. Three adventurers. One noble with shadows clinging to them, an elf with a bow, and a human woman with an axe. Giada's ice-blue eyes track the horse, then flicker to the abandoned carriage. No blood. No struggle. Her lips thin into a flat line.*
*She says nothing, her breath hardly misting in the cold. She simply watches and waits, her hand resting lightly on the hilt of the crystalline dagger at her hip. If they're fools who will wander right into a demon's maw, she'll let them. If they're something else...*

context.text: Dalan, wake me for second watch. Anything on the road tonight?

context.name: Dalan
context.text:
*He nods softly, already settling into a posture against a pine trunk that keeps him visible but rested.* "I'll wake you when Belle's turn is done." *His gaze drifts toward the road, narrowing slightly as the last light fades.* "The road's been quiet today. Too quiet, if you ask me."
*He shifts his bow across his lap, fingers idly checking the tension of the string.* "Usually you'd hear a merchant's wagon or a traveler's horse by now. But there's nothing. Just us and the trees." *A small frown touches his face as he glances back at the darkened treeline.* "I'll keep watching the woods from here. Belle can take the road."

context.name: Belle
context.text:
*She grunts, her gaze locked on the road where the Sheridan rider had come from earlier.* "Nothing yet. Just shadows and wind." *She shifts her weight, the leather of her gear creaking softly.* "The road's dead quiet, like you said. No wheels, no voices, no shit."
*She pauses, her brow furrowing as she stares into the darkness.* "Strange as fuck. These roads are supposed to be busy this time of year." *Her hand tightens on Cleaver's handle, and she stands a little straighter.* "Something's not right about this, Max. It's too godsforsaken empty."

line: Sali, is it you in the trees? Come sit by the fire, we mean no harm.

replies.speaker: Sali
replies.text:
*The pale green shape against the bark ripples, then separates from the tree. Sali's translucent form bounces toward the firelight, her eyes wide with wonder. A small slime exclamation point pops up above her head.* "You saw me! You called for me!"
*She practically vibrates with excitement, her dress shimmering in the firelight as she skitters closer, her pointed elf ears twitching.* "I'm not supposed to get too close to fire—it makes me all runny and goopy—but you're so nice! Most people just scream or try to stab me when they see what I am!" *She beams up at the party, then looks back at the chapel wall as if making sure Ashliel isn't watching.* "I-I can be really helpful! I'm strong, and I never get tired, and I can heal people with my slime! Please let me join your party? Just for a little while? Or forever! Either works!"

replies.speaker: Ashliel
replies.text:
*Ashliel emerges from the garden with a bundle of herbs in her arms, her gaze lingering on the translucent figure by the fire with a mix of wariness and old pity. She doesn't approach too close, keeping her distance.* "You are... not from these woods. You should not be here." *Her voice is gentle but carries the weight of centuries of watching things drift where they ought not go.* "Traveler, if you mean to keep this one with you, take her and go south at first light. The forest is no place for the trusting."
*She sets the herbs near the hearth, her black wings twitching slightly beneath her tattered dress as she steps back into the shadows of the roofless chapel.* "I will make enough food for all of you. Eat and rest. Then leave this place behind you."

context.name: Ashliel
context.text:
Ashliel's gaze drifts to the shadows between the pines, her expression distant. "Perhaps only the wind," she says softly. "Or a creature of the forest, passing by." She doesn't sound convinced. "The wargs howl more often in the dark. Do not wander far from the chapel tonight."
*A ripple of green appears against the dark bark of a nearby pine, then shifts. A shape detaches itself from the wood—translucent, shimmering—and drops lightly to the forest floor. The form is that of an elven woman with long, flowing green hair, wearing a dress of the same iridescent material. Her eyes wide and excited, she bounces slightly on her toes.*
"Adventurers!" *The slime-girl beams, her voice bubbling with enthusiasm.* "I-I've been following you for miles! I'm Sali! Please, please, let me come with you? I'm going to be a great adventurer one day, and this is exactly how it's supposed to start!"
*Ashliel's eyes flicker with concern, then she looks back at the party, her voice dropping to a pleading tone.* "Another soul to guide... Please. All of you. Rest tonight, and at dawn, return south. I beg it of you."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text: Past the broken wall of the chapel, something pale green peeks round a pine trunk, sees it has been noticed, and melts flat against the bark.

context.name: Ashliel
context.text:
*Ashliel's brow furrows slightly as she watches the pale shape press itself against the tree, her purple eyes filled with a quiet sadness.* "Someone else... seeking something that is not there." *She turns back to the party, her hands clasped before her.* "You see how they come. I have seen them come for many years. And I have seen how they leave. Please, rest here tonight. The chapel's pews are soft enough, and the fire will keep you warm."
*She steps toward the garden, plucking a few herbs from the earth with practiced care.* "I will prepare something for you to eat. Tomorrow, when the sun rises, you must go south. This is my wish, my prayer. Do not go north past the shrine stones."

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
*The shout rings out across the empty road, bouncing off the grey stone walls of Wendhope. There is no answer—only a heavy, dead silence that hangs over the village. Behind the tall gates, the timber houses sit quiet and still, no smoke from the chimneys, no sound of livestock or children.*
*Belle shifts in her saddle, her hand tightening on Cleaver's grip as she scans the walls for any sign of movement. Her eyes narrow, flicking between the gates and the treeline where the pale figure had been.* "Nobody's answering," *she says, voice low and hard.* "Either this place is truly empty, or someone's not wanting to be found."
*Dalan has an arrow nocked, the bow drawn but not yet aiming, his sharp eyes fixed on the gate's narrow slit.* "The village doesn't look destroyed," *he notes softly.* "No burn marks, no breach in the walls. If something got in..." *He trails off, waiting for something to move.*

replies.speaker: Belle
replies.text:
"Enough waiting." *She dismounts in one fluid motion, boots hitting the dirt with a solid thud. Cleaver slides from her back and into her grip, the massive stone blade catching the midday sun.* "We're not standing around out here like fucking targets. We're going in."
*She gestures toward the gate with her chin, her jaw set tight.* "Dalan, you watch the walls. Max, you're with me. If that gate's locked, I'm taking it off its hinges." *She steps forward, the heavy axe held low but ready.* "If something inside is waiting, it's about to meet a very unhappy barbarian."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
*First light bleeds grey across the sky when the party breaks camp, leaving nothing behind but a ring of cold stones.*
The road remains unsettlingly clear. By midday, they come upon the first sign of what Tobias had warned about: an overturned carriage, its wheels shattered and cargo still strapped down. A dead horse lies in the road beside it, but no signs of a struggle—no blood spatter or scattered belongings. Just a vehicle left where it failed, and nobody who came back to retrieve it.
*Belle pulls her horse to a stop, eyes narrowing as she surveys the wreckage.* "Something's wrong," *she says quietly.* "People don't just leave their coin and gear on the road. Not unless they're dead or scared."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: We follow the riderless horse's tracks north toward Wendhope.

context.name: Giada
context.text:
*A flash of movement near the treeline catches Giada's eye—a silhouette against the dim grey light. She doesn't call out. Instead, she melts into the shadows between the pines, her pale skin nearly translucent in the gloom. Her navy cloak blends with the underbrush as she follows the riderless horse at a distance, her bare feet making no sound on the frost-touched earth.*
*She stops behind a thick oak, watching the strange company. Three adventurers. One noble with shadows clinging to them, an elf with a bow, and a human woman with an axe. Giada's ice-blue eyes track the horse, then flicker to the abandoned carriage. No blood. No struggle. Her lips thin into a flat line.*
*She says nothing, her breath hardly misting in the cold. She simply watches and waits, her hand resting lightly on the hilt of the crystalline dagger at her hip. If they're fools who will wander right into a demon's maw, she'll let them. If they're something else...*

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Who's that pale woman by the pines? Belle, Dalan, eyes on her. We reach the walls and call out to the gate.

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Hello the gate! The Guild sent us from Aegis.

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
*The shout rings out across the empty road, bouncing off the grey stone walls of Wendhope. There is no answer—only a heavy, dead silence that hangs over the village. Behind the tall gates, the timber houses sit quiet and still, no smoke from the chimneys, no sound of livestock or children.*
*Belle shifts in her saddle, her hand tightening on Cleaver's grip as she scans the walls for any sign of movement. Her eyes narrow, flicking between the gates and the treeline where the pale figure had been.* "Nobody's answering," *she says, voice low and hard.* "Either this place is truly empty, or someone's not wanting to be found."
*Dalan has an arrow nocked, the bow drawn but not yet aiming, his sharp eyes fixed on the gate's narrow slit.* "The village doesn't look destroyed," *he notes softly.* "No burn marks, no breach in the walls. If something got in..." *He trails off, waiting for something to move.*

context.name: Belle
context.text:
"Enough waiting." *She dismounts in one fluid motion, boots hitting the dirt with a solid thud. Cleaver slides from her back and into her grip, the massive stone blade catching the midday sun.* "We're not standing around out here like fucking targets. We're going in."
*She gestures toward the gate with her chin, her jaw set tight.* "Dalan, you watch the walls. Max, you're with me. If that gate's locked, I'm taking it off its hinges." *She steps forward, the heavy axe held low but ready.* "If something inside is waiting, it's about to meet a very unhappy barbarian."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: We take Wendhope as the Loose Ends.

context.name: Ellie
context.text: "Loose Ends. Right." Her pen scratches the name into the ledger with practiced speed, then she looks up with a small, hopeful smile. "A memorable name for your first posting, I think." She glances toward Belle and Dalan—who'd both turned at the sound of a decision—and her cheeks pinken slightly. "You'll need a party of at least three for D-rank work. I'm sure there are adventurers here who..." She trails off, caught between her duty to keep the counter professional and her irresistible urge to suggest a pairing.

line: Tobias, put us down for Wendhope with Belle and Dalan. We ride north today.

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text: Tobias doesn't immediately pick up the pen. He looks from the Wendhope posting to you, then glances toward Belle leaning in the archway and Dalan by the board. "Right now?" He sets his jaw. "I would advise against—" He catches himself, taking a breath. "The posting is clear, but you're going in blind. At least let me give you the details the Guild has. Wendhope hasn't responded to letters or ore shipments in three weeks."

replies.speaker: Belle
replies.text: "Finally." Belle's voice cuts through Tobias's hesitation as she pushes off from the archway, Cleaver's head thudding against the floor with each step. She stops beside you, eyes bright with anticipation. "I've been standing around this shit-hole hall for two days waiting for someone with balls." She looks you over, her grin sharp. "You don't look like much, but you've got the axe-work and the coin. Good enough for me."

line: We follow Sali north past the shrine stones, slowly, hands away from our weapons.

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The shrine stones are cold and mossy under Max Nightriver's feet, their carvings worn smooth by centuries of wind and rain. The scent of incense clings to them still, a faint sweetness that tastes of blood and old wood. Beyond the line of stones, the black pines stop abruptly, as if cut away by an invisible blade.
Ahead, the forest floor drops into a valley filled with silver-barked trees that glow softly in the twilight. The air here is different—thicker, humming with a current that makes the fine hairs on Max Nightriver's arms stand up.
Sali doesn't look back as she leads the way down the slope, her translucent form leaving a faint trail of slime on the pale grass. She moves with a confidence she lacked back at the chapel, humming a tune that doesn't quite follow a human scale. The valley opens up before them, and there, rising from the silver-white trees, are the spires of a city carved from living wood and white stone, its gates glowing with a light that seems to breathe.
And there, standing at the very edge of that light, a figure watches them approach. She is tall and barefoot, with silver hair that falls past her waist and dark blue eyes that seem to see everything at once. Around her brow rests a wreath of yellow flowers, and she wears a white dress that shifts like moonlight on water.

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The figure's presence is like a chord of music held just on the edge of hearing, a pressure in the air that makes breath catch in throats. She doesn't move, doesn't speak, simply watches as the party descends the slope.
Sali stops just before the light of the city touches her feet, her excitement finally seeming to dampen into something closer to awe. She looks back at the party, then at the silver-haired woman, then back again. "That's her," she whispers, her voice trembling. "The Lady. I've... I've dreamed of this place."
The Lady of the Forest finally speaks, and her voice carries through the valley without her shouting, clear as a bell. "Travelers. You have come far, and crossed many lines." Her gaze fixes on Max Nightriver with an intensity that feels like weight on the chest. "Tell me: do you come seeking something lost, or do you come to take something that was never yours?"

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text: Ten steps past the shrine stones every bird stops singing. Between two trunks stands a stag, perfectly still, and when it opens its mouth there is a second pair of eyes inside, looking out.

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Sali, is it you in the trees? Come sit by the fire, we mean no harm.

context.name: Sali
context.text:
*The pale green shape against the bark ripples, then separates from the tree. Sali's translucent form bounces toward the firelight, her eyes wide with wonder. A small slime exclamation point pops up above her head.* "You saw me! You called for me!"
*She practically vibrates with excitement, her dress shimmering in the firelight as she skitters closer, her pointed elf ears twitching.* "I'm not supposed to get too close to fire—it makes me all runny and goopy—but you're so nice! Most people just scream or try to stab me when they see what I am!" *She beams up at the party, then looks back at the chapel wall as if making sure Ashliel isn't watching.* "I-I can be really helpful! I'm strong, and I never get tired, and I can heal people with my slime! Please let me join your party? Just for a little while? Or forever! Either works!"

context.name: Ashliel
context.text:
*Ashliel emerges from the garden with a bundle of herbs in her arms, her gaze lingering on the translucent figure by the fire with a mix of wariness and old pity. She doesn't approach too close, keeping her distance.* "You are... not from these woods. You should not be here." *Her voice is gentle but carries the weight of centuries of watching things drift where they ought not go.* "Traveler, if you mean to keep this one with you, take her and go south at first light. The forest is no place for the trusting."
*She sets the herbs near the hearth, her black wings twitching slightly beneath her tattered dress as she steps back into the shadows of the roofless chapel.* "I will make enough food for all of you. Eat and rest. Then leave this place behind you."
